newsitem.title: USA: U.S. propane slightly higher amid weak crude oil.
newsitem.headline: U.S. propane slightly higher amid weak crude oil.

text.p: U.S. prices of propane edged up in moderate to slow trade late on Tuesday amid some buying interest in the Midwest, players said.
Traders said end-users in the Conway, Kansas, hub came out to buy material to meet immediate demand.
The U.S. Gulf Coast also met with petrochemical interest, although at lower levels than earlier in the week.
In late trade, Conway anytime propane rose a half cent to between 38.50 cents and 39.00 cents a gallon, with deals done within the range.
Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot material also rose, about a quarter cent to 37.00/37.50 cents. Deals went as high as 38.00 cents but started to drift with NYMEX crude oil.
March crude ended down 4 at $22.42 a barrel.
The ethane markets also continued to slip in a downtrend amid weak demand.
